The students also expressed solidarity with NALSAR students and faculty over the BCI’s actions, including its directions to the university to identify students and faculty members who had participated in a representation. items.title: CAG report says not even half of emergency disaster funds transferred to states
items.summary: The Union government has not spent even half of the funds under the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), meant for meeting expenses for emergency response related to disasters. More than 53% of funds, which would supplement the State Disaster Response Funds, remains unutilised, as per a report of Comptroller and Auditor General of India based on the accounts of Union government in 2024-25, tabled at the Parliament the other day. Of the total Rs 11,474 crore sanctioned under NDRF as assistance to the state for calamities of severe nature, only Rs 5356 crore was transferred to the states. The remaining Rs 6117.97 crore is listed as ‘savings’ in the CAG report to indicate that it was unspent. This comes at a time when several states, including Kerala and Assam, are alleging that the Union government ignored its demand for more NRDF funds during devastating natural calamities. CAG has noted this glaring disparity in the head ‘Transfers to state’, which also include assistance to state from National Disaster Mitigation Funds (NDMF) and special assistance. items.title: Nithin Raj suicide: Kerala HC suspects bid by police to shield accused
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has questioned the conduct of the police in the investigation into the death of Nithin Raj, a student of Anjarakandy Dental College, stating that the sequence of events raises suspicion that senior officials tried to protect the prime accused, Dr MK Ram. Justice A Badharudeen, on July 22, Wednesday, while hearing a petition filed by Nithin's parents, observed that the manner in which Ram, a former faculty member of the college, was arrested appeared to have paved the way for his release on bail. The court said the mandatory safeguards laid down by the Supreme Court during arrest did not appear to have been followed, raising serious doubts about the police's handling of the case. The court ordered a thorough inquiry into the circumstances that led to Ram securing bail from the Thalassery Special Court dealing with cases under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. It cautioned that if the police failed to conduct a credible probe, the High Court would consider initiating its own inquiry, which could include scrutiny of the phone records of those allegedly involved. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Activists monitoring the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Telangana have urged the Election Commission to give a chance to challenge any wrongful categorisations under the Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others (ASDDO) or ‘uncollectable’ tag. Telangana Chief Electoral Officer C Sudarshan Reddy had recently announced that by the end of the enumeration period which concluded on August 10, around 73.39 lakh enumeration forms, or 21.70% of the total voters in the state, were classified as “uncollectable”. Of these, 9.22 lakh voters were marked as dead, 11.25 lakh were classified as absent or untraceable, 45.18 lakh voters were found to have permanently shifted, while 6.70 lakh were marked as already enrolled. Around 1.02 lakh voters were listed under the ‘others’ category. While the draft electoral roll is set to be published on August 17, activists SQ Masood and MA Mujeeb argued that such a large number of electors need additional safeguards before being potentially deleted. items.title: Mamata Banerjee’s aide Ashish Banerjee found dead at TMC office in Birbhum
items.summary: Former West Bengal Assembly Deputy Speaker and veteran Trinamool Congress leader Ashish Banerjee was found dead inside a party office adjoining his residence in Rampurhat, Birbhum, on Sunday, August 16, with police recovering a purported suicide note from the spot. A large crowd gathered outside the office and his residence after news of his death spread. Banerjee’s body was sent for post-mortem examination. Birbhum Superintendent of Police Vidit Raj Bhundesh told The Indian Express that it was “primarily” a suicide case and that a note had been recovered. The officer said the note stated: “No one is responsible for my death.” The purported note, written in Bengali on Banerjee’s letterhead, contained his denial of corruption allegations and references to his political career. It reportedly said : “I was never involved in corruption. It was a blunder to join politics.” He also expressed regret over entering politics and advised younger members of his family to stay away from politics and concentrate on their professions. The note also reportedly addressed his role in the Tarapith Rampurhat Development Authority (TRDA). He said he had no substantial responsibilities in the authority

items.title: Andhra women availed 87 crore fare-free bus rides in first year of Stree Shakti scheme
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. As Andhra Pradesh’s fare-free bus travel scheme for women, Stree Shakti, completed one year on August 15, officials said that on average, women avail 24 lakh bus rides under the scheme daily. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu travelled in an RTC bus on August 15 from the Parade Ground to Camp Office in the Amaravati region and interacted with a few women passengers. A total of 87 crore fare-free bus rides have been completed in one year of the scheme being in effect, Naidu said, making the daily average around 24 lakh rides. The Stree Shakti scheme is currently being implemented in 7,631 Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) buses, covering about 76% of the corporation’s fleet, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. The government is subsidising bus fares worth around Rs 8.53 crore a day, amounting to a total of Rs 3,095 crore so far, the statement said. It also noted that after the scheme was introduced, women’s occupancy in RTC buses increased to 62%. Naidu stated that through the Stree Shakti scheme, women are getting to save money, and use those savings for family and livelih
